original_question: For a plurisubharmonic function phi on a bounded pseudoconvex domain, determine what can be said about the set of points where phi admits no differential test from above; in particular, determine whether that set has zero Lebesgue measure or zero capacity.
target_in_paper: Section 6.1, Question 39 (Guedj-Zeriahi): the local viscosity-theoretic question about the set of points where a plurisubharmonic function fails to admit a differential test from above.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely. It correctly identifies the ambient local setting of a bounded pseudoconvex domain, the object φ being plurisubharmonic, the exceptional set where φ admits no differential test from above, and the paper's specific follow-up asks about whether that set has zero Lebesgue measure or zero capacity.
missing_details: The paper first fixes the ambient setting as a bounded pseudoconvex domain Ω \subset \mathbb{C}^n (for example, the unit ball), and the question is local inside this fixed domain.
The phrase 'admits a differential test from above at z' should be defined explicitly: there must exist a neighborhood V of z and a C^2 function q on V such that (φ - q)(z) = sup_V (φ - q).
The exceptional set should be written explicitly as E_φ := { z ∈ Ω : φ does not admit a differential test from above at z }.
Question 39 imposes no extra regularity or boundedness assumptions on φ beyond plurisubharmonicity; in particular, it does not assume continuity, local boundedness, or membership in DMA(Ω).
The paper records the known partial result that E_φ has empty interior; including this makes the question more faithful to the original formulation.

The paper says 'zero Lebesgue measure (or capacity)' but does not define the capacity notion in the immediate nearby text, so a stand-alone rewrite should either preserve that wording or explicitly name the intended pluripotential capacity.
refined_question: Let Ω \subset \mathbb{C}^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain, and let φ ∈ PSH(Ω). For z ∈ Ω, say that φ admits a differential test from above at z if there exist a neighborhood V of z and a C^2-smooth function q on V such that (φ - q)(z) = sup_V (φ - q). If E_φ := { z ∈ Ω : φ does not admit a differential test from above at z }, what can be said about E_φ? In particular, although E_φ is known to have empty interior, must E_φ have zero Lebesgue measure, or even zero capacity?
justification: This is the exact official problem your draft is aiming at. Section 6.1 fixes the local setting Ω \subset \mathbb{C}^n, Definition 6.1 gives the precise meaning of a differential test from above, and Question 39 then asks verbatim about the set of points where a plurisubharmonic function does not admit such a test, followed immediately by the more specific query whether that set has zero Lebesgue measure or capacity. The only substantial additions needed to make your draft fully stand-alone are the precise test-function definition, the explicit description of the exceptional set, and the recorded partial result that the set has empty interior.
